section.name: PierLevelSeatCheck
section.heading: Level pier bearing seats — rotation check
section.paragraph: Evaluate level tops at the four pier bearings, B1/B2 for Span 1 and B3/B4 for Span 2. This check uses the selected Type F pads and the saved beam-end rotations. It does not change pedestal geometry or approve the end-bent seats.

paragraph.link: FDOT SPI 400-510, FY 2026–27, pp. 1–2 — Type F limits and level-seat allowance
FDOT Structures Design Guidelines, January 2026, §6.5.1.D — bearing seats and rotations

section.paragraph: SDG's general detailing rule uses level seats below 0.5% grade and seats parallel to the beam from 0.5% to 2%. SPI 400-510 additionally permits level seats where the combined grade, camber and dead-load rotation remains within its static limit. The specific combined-rotation allowance is evaluated here. No beveled plate is required by the longitudinal grade alone; the standard embedded beam plate remains part of the beam detail.

textcell.paragraph: Determine whether the selected pads can accommodate level pier seats.
Live profile/pad/thermal inputs and selected Mathcad saved end rotations.
Pier rotation, direction and longitudinal movement screens; explicit remaining checks.

section.paragraph: Positive beam slope rises with increasing station. Saved Mathcad camber slopes are positive at the left end; downward DL/LL slopes are negative. Reverse their signs at the right end of Span 1 (pier); retain them at the left end of Span 2 (pier). Beam self-weight is already included in the camber result. The 2% deck crossfall is taken in the haunch; transverse beam tilt is assumed zero and must be maintained in detailing.

The selected 12 October 2026 Span 1/Span 2 Mathcad worksheets supply Slope&Defl, region 202056, in degrees and inches. These are saved external analysis results, not a new native Mathcad run. Refresh these source inputs if either beam analysis changes. Direct end rotations govern; 4 × net midspan camber / span would discard the actual curvature distribution.

section.heading: Adopted bearing-seat geometry: level as-cast bearing seats at all supports
section.paragraph: Design decision (20 October 2026): level as-cast pedestal tops at all supports, each at the maximum elevation of its original top. Maximum means the highest point of each original pedestal top, not the highest support elevation across the bridge. Each pedestal is a solid with one horizontal top face; pads are uniform thickness and level on that face.

section.paragraph: Elevations use the existing model datum and are stored at native precision; both pedestals at a support share the listed value. Caps, beam profile/camber, deck and all other geometry are unchanged. The pad thickness is retained; no taper, compression or beveled plate is invented.

Reinforcement: retain all 84 pedestal bars at their prior elevations, with their native links and adopted marks. A separate pre-grinding reference prevents later regeneration from lifting the cages into the grinding allowance. Verify cover against the final approved ground surface.

Independent undeformed CAD fit: every pad has positive-volume interference with its unchanged beam. Maximum sampled vertical differences at pad ends/centers are EB1 0.124029 in, Pier 0.046051 in, and EB2 0.157234 in. These measurements describe the current rigid geometry; they are not specified grinding depths or an elastic bearing response. Final fit remains FAIL until an accepted support detail resolves the interface.

Construction intent: cast level stock at the listed maximum elevations and establish any required grinding plane and final seat elevation before final pad setting. Recheck remaining pedestal thickness, reinforcement cover, surface flatness, support contact and erection/service conditions. Grinding is not an automatic approval to remove arbitrary depth or to modify a loaded support.

Bearing basis: the pier level-seat check above (PierLevelSeatCheck) applies with its signed rotations, saved analysis assumptions and limitations. Its conditional pier rotation/movement result does not approve the end bents or close combined shear, uplift/contact, load/source currency, final bearing detailing or construction-stage checks. This is a geometry override, not final bearing acceptance.
